summary: The Nelson Mandela scholarships are part of the South-South Cooperation programme of AGCID, the Chilean government's international cooperation agency. They fund master's (magister) studies at accredited Chilean universities and other higher education institutions from the 2027 academic year for professionals, public officials and academics of ten African countries: Angola, Algeria, Botswana, Egypt, Ethiopia, Ghana, Kenya, Morocco, Mozambique and South Africa. The programme began in 2014 and has supported more than 160 African professionals. The award pays return flights, tuition, a monthly allowance, insurance and two smaller grants for up to 24 months.
eligibility_notes:
Applicants must be nationals of Angola, Algeria, Botswana, Egypt, Ethiopia, Ghana, Kenya, Morocco, Mozambique or South Africa and hold a professional title or degree. Basic Spanish, oral and written, is an essential requirement, because master's programmes in Chile are taught only in Spanish; the application needs an official document from the applicant's country's embassy certifying Spanish proficiency.

Applicants must first get unconditional acceptance into a master's programme on the call's Annex 1 list, at their own cost, at a Chilean institution. Programmes must be full-time with exclusive dedication; a programme with other characteristics is not considered. In-person and hybrid study gets priority.

Priority goes to candidates presented by public officials or academics of universities officially recognised by their country, to programmes on the Annex 1 list, and to postgraduate programmes in themes Chile considers relevant: astronomy, mining, Antarctic sciences, renewable energy, marine resources, economic development, international trade, international relations, sovereignty, integrity of territory and national security, and the fight against organised crime and terrorism. The AGCID programme page describes the target group as professionals and academics in the public sector, higher education or NGOs working in areas such as public-sector modernisation, policy management, productive-sector development and food security.

Not accepted: foreigners who already hold a residence or work visa for Chile; applicants whose spouse holds this or another AGCID scholarship (if both spouses apply, only one can get an award). The scholarship cannot be combined with any other postgraduate scholarship the person holds or has obtained from Chilean government bodies. A person who got an AGCID postgraduate scholarship must wait five years after it ended before applying for another postgraduate one (three years for a short specialised course). AGCID's programme page says MBAs and medical specialisations are not funded.
age_experience_notes: No minimum or maximum age and no minimum years of experience are required. They only change the score: age 36 to 50 scores 100, under 35 scores 50 and over 51 scores 20; five years or more of professional experience in the field of the studies scores 100, 3 to under 5 years 65, 6 months to 3 years 35, and none 5.
funding_summary: The scholarship pays the return airfare from the capital of the home country to the study city (a bus ticket if the city has no airport), tuition, enrolment and graduation costs up to four academic semesters or six trimesters, a monthly allowance of CLP 600,000, life, health and accident insurance in Chile, a one-time CLP 90,000 study materials grant and a one-time CLP 300,000 thesis grant. Funding lasts up to 24 months. The call lists these as the only benefits; visa costs, university application costs, airport taxes and trips home during the scholarship are the scholar's own. Studies may start between 1 March and 30 September 2027.
programmes_note: Only full-time master's programmes on the call's Annex 1 list, taught in Spanish, at accredited Chilean institutions can be funded. There is no fixed subject list, but the call prioritises: astronomy, mining, Antarctic sciences, renewable energy, marine resources, economic development, international trade, international relations, sovereignty and national security, and fighting organised crime and terrorism. The programme page says MBAs and medical specialisations are excluded. In-person and hybrid programmes are preferred. The Annex 1 list could not be read, so no individual programmes are listed here.
institutions_note: Accredited Chilean universities and other higher education institutions with master's programmes on the Annex 1 list. Applicants contact the admissions offices themselves and should ask in writing about requirements, prior skills, emphasis and the curriculum. Applications to universities in regions of Chile outside Santiago score higher (100 points against 50 for the Metropolitan Region).

summary.detail: Master's (magister) programmes from the Annex 1 list, taught only in Spanish, full-time with exclusive dedication, with up to 24 months of funding. Studies may start between 1 March and 30 September 2027; classes may begin from the first week of March 2027, so selected candidates must be able to travel to Chile from 1 March 2027. Requires a professional title or degree, basic Spanish and unconditional acceptance into the programme.

benefits.limit_text: One-way airfare from the capital of the home country to the final study city on arrival in Chile, and the return airfare to the capital at the end of studies; a bus ticket if the study city has no airport
benefits.conditions: Not applicable to scholars who study the whole programme remotely or online.

benefits.limit_text: Tuition, enrolment and graduation costs of the programme, up to four academic semesters or six trimesters, within 24 months maximum
benefits.conditions: Only costs belonging to the academic curriculum of the programme for which the scholarship was granted.

benefits.limit_text: CLP 600,000 per month for the length of the studies, up to 24 months
benefits.conditions: In December, January and/or February the scholar needs AGCID's approval of any trip out of the country to receive 100% of that month's allowance. The first payment needs the Chilean identity card (about 30 days), so the scholar needs own funds for the first weeks. Not for online scholars.

benefits.limit_text: Life, health and accident insurance for events inside Chile while the scholarship lasts, and access to Chilean public health services once the scholar has the Chilean identity card
benefits.conditions: Not for scholars who study entirely online.

benefits.limit_text: One-time grant of CLP 90,000 for books and study materials
benefits.conditions: Paid within the first academic period. Not for online scholars.

benefits.limit_text: One-time thesis support grant of CLP 300,000
benefits.conditions: Paid only if the grade average in the programme is 5.5 or equivalent or higher. Before the end of the 19th month of the allowance, the scholar must show the signed thesis schedule, the approved thesis project and a grade certificate.

benefits.limit_text: Visa procedures, application costs to Chilean institutions, airport boarding taxes and similar charges, and trips home during the scholarship are paid by the scholar
benefits.conditions: The call lists its benefits as the only ones; any other expense is the scholar's. The benefits are for the scholar only, not for family.

requirements.text: AGCID scholarship application form, filled in on a computer and signed.

Definitive acceptance letter from the Chilean institution for the chosen programme, showing unconditional acceptance, the study mode (in person, hybrid or online), the start and end dates including thesis and final exam, and the enrolment fee and annual tuition. The cost of getting the letter is the applicant's.
Health certificate from a licensed doctor listing pre-existing conditions declared by the applicant (the call's Annex 5 declaration).
Professional title certificate or a copy certified by a notary. If selected, it must be apostilled or legalised in the country that issued it.
CV with emphasis on work and academic background.
Short description of the reasons for studying in Chile, the aims of the studies and how the applicant will use them after returning home.
Short description of the likely thesis area and topic.

Sponsorship letter from the employer, stating the employer's interest in the studies in Chile, that the applicant has permission to be absent for the whole scholarship, and whether the job will be kept on return.
Official document from the applicant's country's embassy certifying proficiency in Spanish (basic oral and written Spanish is required).

All documents are in Spanish, scanned and legible, in electronic format, and are submitted to the Chilean embassy in the applicant's country (or the embassy of a country covering it) listed in Annex 3, which enters them on AGCID's scholarship platform. Beneficiaries are subject to Chile's migration law.

application_steps.title: Check eligibility and get unconditional acceptance from a Chilean university
application_steps.detail: You need a professional title, basic oral and written Spanish, and the definitive acceptance letter for a full-time master's on the Annex 1 list, with study mode, dates, enrolment fee and annual tuition. The admission and its costs are your responsibility; ask the university in writing about requirements and curriculum. You must not hold a Chilean residence or work visa.

application_steps.title: Prepare the documents and submit them to the Chilean embassy
application_steps.detail: Prepare the signed application form, acceptance letter, health certificate with the Annex 5 declaration, title certificate, CV, motivation description, thesis topic, academic reference, employer sponsorship letter if employed, and the embassy's Spanish proficiency document. Submit them electronically, in Spanish, to the Chilean embassy in your country (or the covering embassy in Annex 3). The embassy's own deadline must be checked with the embassy. Missing or false documents cause immediate elimination.

application_steps.title: The embassy enters pre-selected candidates in AGCID's platform
application_steps.detail: The embassy or focal point enters the pre-selected candidates in AGCID's scholarship platform. The platform closed on 30 October 2026 at 23:59 Chile time; applications sent after that are automatically out of the selection.

application_steps.title: National pre-selection by a joint committee
application_steps.detail: A joint pre-selection committee of the national focal point and an official of the Chilean embassy chooses candidates on technical criteria and may interview them. Each country ranks its pre-selected candidates in priority order, and they compete for places with candidates from the other countries.

application_steps.title: Final selection by AGCID's selection committee in Chile
application_steps.detail: Only complete applications are considered. Weights are: country priority 20%, alignment with Chile's foreign-policy priorities 15%, professional experience 25%, public or private employer 10%, gender 10% (women score higher), age 5% and region of the Chilean university 5%, followed by an overall judgement. The decision cannot be appealed and is told to the applicants and to both countries' ambassadors, from the second half of November 2026.

application_steps.title: Sign the acceptance document, get permission and the student visa
application_steps.detail: The award takes effect when you sign AGCID's scholarship acceptance document. Get your employer's permission if you are employed, and apply online for the Chilean student visa straight after selection, because it can take up to two months; send AGCID a copy of the visa approval. You may start the visa once you have the definitive acceptance letter, which does not oblige AGCID to award the scholarship.

application_steps.title: Travel to Chile and settle in
application_steps.detail: Classes can start from the first week of March 2027, so be able to travel from 1 March 2027, and arrive about 3 to 5 working days before the programme starts. Bring enough money for personal costs for about the first 30 days, until the Chilean identity card is issued and the first allowance can be collected. Set your home address in the study city within three working days of arrival.

application_steps.title: Meet the scholar's duties, finish and return home
application_steps.detail: Scholars must live in the study city, study exclusively and take no paid work in Chile or abroad, pass every course with a grade average of at least 5.0 each period, report trips and return dates to AGCID, hand in the final thesis copy and acknowledge AGCID in academic work. Failing courses can suspend the allowance; serious breaches end the scholarship and require repaying benefits other than insurance, and bar future AGCID scholarships. After the full programme the scholar must return to the home country.

not_stated: The Annex 1 list of eligible master's programmes and institutions, and the Annex 3 list of embassies and focal points with national deadlines: not in the call text read.
A minimum Spanish test or score: only an embassy document certifying basic Spanish is required.
A minimum grade average for applicants and the number of scholarships offered.
A maximum age or minimum years of work experience (they only affect the score).
A closing time for national applications at the embassy: it must be checked with the embassy.
fetch_problems: The AGCID current-offers page showed no call details or annexes when read; the convocatorias page loads its content by script.
Annexes 1 to 5 were not available as separate files, so the programme list and the embassy list were not read.
notes: The AGCID programme page names priority areas for this scholarship (public-sector modernisation, policy management, productive-sector development, food security), while the 2027 call lists other themes (astronomy, mining, Antarctic sciences, renewable energy, marine resources, economic development, international trade, international relations, national security, organised crime and terrorism). Both are described above.
The selection weights listed in the call add up to 90%, although the call writes a total of 100%.
The call says applications go to the Chilean embassy (or covering embassy); the AGCID programme page says applications go through the national focal point. The call text names the embassy route.

The stored amounts and countries match the 2027 call; stored text that said 'details are from the 2026 call' is now replaced by the 2027 text. The stored study period (3 March 2027 to 28 February 2029) was not re-read; the call itself says studies may start between 1 March and 30 September 2027.
